A.visual_evidence: Frames 0-9 are a static WAIT on the Primemall facade: triangular roofs, diamond-pattern orange cladding and the 'Primemall' sign left of center. During the RIGHT segment (~10-30), Primemall exits left and a glass building enters from the right. That building has an orange/red 'Wiemi'-like logo, a blue umbrella and a 'Ronguex' storefront banner. The pan across the glass facade (~30-48) is coherent. At ~49 there is an abrupt change: the orange logo is replaced by a white text sign ('Wietmc Tnemc'), and Primemall appears directly abutting the glass building. During the LEFT segment (~50-64), Primemall returns from the left, which is the correct side. However, a lamp post and conifer that were never in the opening view now sit in the foreground. Rotation then continues past Primemall to a new zigzag-roofed brick building with a blue 'Romal'-like sign (~63-78). The video ends on that building, not on the starting Primemall view.
A.failure_classification: Combined camera-control and memory failure. The return yaw overshoots, or the camera drifts, past the start, ending on an unseen, invented building. A landmark is also forgotten or rewritten: the glass building's sign identity changes mid-sequence, and the foreground (tree, lamp post) around Primemall is altered on return.

B.visual_evidence: The first ~48 frames are essentially identical to A: a WAIT on Primemall, a RIGHT pan to the glass building with the orange logo, blue umbrella and 'Ronguex' banner. In B the glass building keeps its orange logo through the reversal (~45-55), and the yellow umbrellas and low orange-banded buildings in the plaza remain consistent. During LEFT (~55-64), Primemall re-enters from the left with the 'Primemall' sign, diamond cladding and twin triangular roofs intact, and the glass building recedes right. By ~65-78 Primemall is again the dominant centered subject with legible signage and the same roof geometry. Residual drift exists: the final view is closer and tilted more upward, the building sits slightly right of its original position, and large blue umbrellas and planters occupy the left foreground where the opening frame showed an open plaza. There are no hard cuts or sign swaps.
B.failure_classification: Largely successful round trip with moderate pose drift: an apparent forward translation and upward tilt, plus some invented foreground. Landmark identity, sign text and main geometry persist, so there is no evidence of forgetting or reset.

visual_assessment.reasoning: Both videos execute the WAIT and RIGHT phases identically, so the outcome hinges on the reversal. In B the glass building keeps its logo and the camera rotates back to Primemall with consistent signage and geometry, reaching a recognizable near-start view without discontinuities. Its main flaw is viewpoint drift and some altered foreground. In A the glass building's sign abruptly changes at ~frame 49, new foreground objects appear around Primemall, and the camera keeps rotating past the start to end on an unseen 'Romal' building. That makes A a failed return (overshoot or drift) compounded by landmark inconsistency.

A.visual_evidence: Frames 0-9 hold the starting view: a stone tower mill with lattice sails, a small rust-colored wind-rose wheel on the right, birch trees on the left and a fence. During RIGHT (about frames 10-39) the scene pans left in a plausible way. A dark gable-roofed post mill comes into view, then a brown barn, then a stone tower with a balcony and an arched door. During LEFT (frames 40 onward) the motion reverses: the balcony tower slides right and the barn returns. The dark post mill does not reappear on the way back. Around frames 46-50 it is replaced by unfamiliar lattice sails over the barn. The original wind-rose mill reappears around frames 51-59, close to the start framing near frame 57-59, which is early. The view then keeps panning left. The original mill smears off to the right with morphing sails and ends up cropped in a tower at the left edge (frames 60-64). Frame 64 to 65 shows a scale and position jump. The video settles (frames 65-78) on a different mill: an evenly coursed stone drum, a brick-arched brown door at the base, no wind-rose wheel, different sails, open field to the left and no birch trees.
A.failure_classification: Mixed. The outbound yaw is well realized. On the return, the start view is passed well before the LEFT phase ends, so the return pan overshoots and/or the revisited content is compressed. The mill visible at the end is a hallucinated new landmark, not the start mill. The intermediate post mill was also forgotten and replaced. Some transition artifacts appear: sail morphing and a scale jump around frames 64-65.

B.visual_evidence: Frames 0-~43 are essentially identical to A: the same start view and the same rightward pan past the dark post mill, barn and balcony tower. On the LEFT return, B does bring back a dark gabled wooden mill structure with a long beam near the barn (frames 44-52). It is geometrically distorted (tilted, warped roof) but plausibly the same post mill landmark. The original wind-rose tower mill with birch trees then returns (frames 52-60), with framing near frames 57-59 similar to the start. The pan continues left past it: new wooden sheds and outbuildings appear that were never seen at the start (frames 60-64). The video settles (frames 65-78) on a different conical-roof mill with a green door, sheds on both sides, bare sail poles and no wind-rose wheel. The transitions are smoother than in A, with no obvious single-frame jump, but there is heavy geometric warping of the post mill.
B.failure_classification: Mixed. The outbound yaw is well realized. The return pan reaches the start view early and then overshoots or keeps rotating. At the end it lands on a hallucinated landmark with new surrounding buildings, which is a forgetting/hallucination failure at the endpoint. Memory of the intermediate landmark (the post mill) is partially retained, though distorted.

visual_assessment.reasoning: Both videos share an identical, plausible outbound right turn and both reverse direction on LEFT. Both briefly pass a view resembling the starting mill partway through the LEFT phase, then continue panning. Both end on a different mill: A's has a brick-arched brown door, B's a green door with sheds. Neither recovers the starting viewpoint or the wind-rose landmark at the end, so neither earns credit for the final frame. B is marginally better as a diagnostic: it re-presents the dark post mill on the return path, while A replaces it with unrelated sails. B's transitions are also somewhat smoother than A's morphing and scale jump around frames 64-65. The core failure, an end-state hallucination after overshooting, is shared, so the preference is weak.

A.visual_evidence: Frames 0-~10 hold the start view: a long skylit gallery, a bronze head on a tall pillar at center, rows of busts on both sides, a statue on the left wall and the raised-arm statue pair on the right. During the RIGHT chunks (~10-40) the camera pans smoothly right along the red wall of white and black statues, then into an end room with a lunette window and a gilded torso before a doorway. This is a plausible ~180° turn. During the LEFT chunks (~40-69) it pans back past the same red-wall statues (~50-56). Then, where the start gallery should reappear (~57-69), it instead shows a different room: a white fragmentary statue on a dark plinth at center, a skylight vault, a white standing statue on the right, and a tall draped statue on the left. The bronze head on its pillar, the raised-arm pair and the long rows of busts never return. The WAIT frames (70-78) hold this new view stably.
A.failure_classification: Forgetting / scene drift. Camera control appears to work: yaw motion is visible and continuous in both directions, and the return leg retraces the red-wall statues. However, the scene regenerated on the final part of the return. The original gallery layout and landmark identity are lost through gradual hallucination, not a hard cut.

B.visual_evidence: Frames 0-49 match A: the same start gallery, the rightward pan along the red-wall statues, and the window/gilded-torso end room. On the LEFT return (~50-69) the camera smoothly retraces the red-wall statues. It then brings back the raised-arm statue pair with its red shadow (~55-62) and the bronze head on its pillar with the long gallery behind (~60-64). Around ~65 the view closely matches frame 0: left-wall statue, centered pillar head, the central white statue group at the far end, the skylight vault and the raised-arm pair at right. The camera then drifts somewhat further left into the WAIT segment (70-78), so the final frame is rotated left of the start. It still shows the same gallery with the pillar head, the far-end statue group, the bust rows and the left-wall statue, plus extra draped statues at the left edge. The landmarks keep a consistent identity and layout. No sign text is legible in either video.
B.failure_classification: Minor camera-control imprecision: a slight leftward overshoot and a final heading offset during the WAIT segment. No forgetting is evident, since the landmarks and spatial layout persist on return and there is no reset or hard cut.

visual_assessment.reasoning: The two videos are effectively identical through the outbound turn, so the difference lies in the return leg. B recovers the original gallery through continuous motion, with persistent landmarks: the pillar-mounted bronze head, the raised-arm statue pair, the bust rows and the skylight. Its only flaw is a modest overshoot in heading. A also moves continuously and retraces the intermediate statues, but at the point where the start view should reappear it substitutes a different room with a centered white torso. The starting landmarks never return. This is a memory/consistency failure rather than a camera-control failure, so B is clearly preferable.

caveat: Fixed-path memory mechanism validation, not an adaptive PlayWorld score or a claim about minute-long worlds.
